court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Addl. District Judge, Fast Track Court III, Trivellore, C.M.A.No.14 of 2008
facts_of_case: The parties got married in 1995 and lived separately for about 25 years. The husband filed a petition for divorce under Section 13(1)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, which was dismissed by the trial court. The appeal is against this dismissal.

legal_principles.principle: When there is no possibility of reunion for several years and the marriage becomes a total failure, then there is no point in declining the relief of divorce to either party approaching the Court.
legal_principles.held: This Court is of the considered opinion that when there is no possibility of reunion for several years and the marriage became a total failure, then, there is no point in declining the relief of divorce to either of the parties approaching the Court of law.

legal_principles.principle: Courts ought to consider the ground of desertion when it is admitted between parties during the course of trial.
legal_principles.held: The Courts ought to have considered the said ground for granting divorce.

outcome.final_order: The Court held that the Courts below erred in not considering the admitted fact regarding desertion as a main ground for divorce under the Hindu Marriage Act.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Section 13(1)(ib)
advising on grounds for divorce in Hindu Marriage Act cases
